title: Generative Design and AI-Aided Modelling
welcome_lead: Software explores thousands of design options against your constraints.

final_note: Designer sets constraints; algorithm explores the space.

concepts.def: Algorithm-driven exploration of design alternatives against constraints.
Removing material from non-load-bearing regions to reduce weight.
Designer-set requirement (load, fixed face, manufacturing limit).
Internal repeating geometry reducing mass while retaining stiffness.

walkthroughs.body_html: Generative design (Autodesk, nTopology) takes a designer's constraints (loads, supports, keep-out volumes) and objective (e.g. minimise mass) and produces dozens of candidate geometries — often organic in appearance.

Topology optimisation iteratively removes material from a starting volume where stress is low, leaving a load-bearing skeleton. Combined with additive manufacturing, it produces parts impossible to machine.

Airbus's 2015 'Bionic Partition' for the A320 cabin was generated using bionic algorithms and printed in scalmalloy (Al-Mg-Sc alloy), saving 45% mass — about 30 kg per partition, hundreds of tonnes of fuel over a lifetime.
